The '''Richtmyer–Meshkov instability (RMI)''' occurs when two fluids of different density are impulsively accelerated.  Normally this is by the passage of a [[shock wave]]. The development of the [[instability]] begins with small amplitude perturbations which initially grow linearly with time. This is followed by a nonlinear regime with bubbles appearing in the case of a light fluid penetrating a heavy fluid, and with spikes appearing in the case of a heavy fluid penetrating a light fluid. A chaotic regime is reached eventually and the two fluids mix. 

This instability can be considered the impulsive-acceleration limit of the [[Rayleigh–Taylor instability]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhou |first1=Ye |title=Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer–Meshkov instabilities: A journey through scales |journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena |date=September 2021 |volume=423 |article-number=132838 |doi=10.1016/j.physd.2020.132838 |bibcode=2021PhyD..42332838Z |hdl=10871/124449 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167278920308393#! |access-date=15 July 2022|hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== History ==
[[Robert D. Richtmyer|R. D. Richtmyer]] provided a theoretical prediction,<ref>{{cite journal |first=Robert D. |last=Richtmyer |title=Taylor Instability in a Shock Acceleration of Compressible Fluids |journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics |volume=13 |issue= 2|pages=297–319 |year=1960 |doi=10.1002/cpa.3160130207 |url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc1257762/ }}</ref> and E. E. Meshkov (Евгений Евграфович Мешков)<sup>([[:ru:Мешков, Евгений Евграфович|ru]])</sup> provided experimental verification.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Instability of the Interface of Two Gases Accelerated by a Shock Wave |journal=Soviet Fluid Dynamics |volume=4 |issue=5 |pages=101–104 |year=1969 |doi=10.1007/BF01015969 |bibcode=1969FlDy....4e.101M |last1=Meshkov |first1=E. E |s2cid=123494913 }}</ref>  Materials in the cores of stars, like Cobalt-56 from [[SN 1987A|Supernova 1987A]] were observed earlier than expected.  This was evidence of mixing due to Richtmyer–Meshkov and [[Rayleigh–Taylor instability|Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities]]. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Richtmyer meshkov instability |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/unsupported_browser}}</ref>

== In magnetohydrodynamics ==
Here are the [[Dispersion relation|dispersion relations]] for ideal [[magnetohydrodynamics]] (MHD):

<math>(\omega^2 - 2k_\parallel ^2 / \beta )(\omega ^4 - (2/ \beta  + 1)k^2 \omega^2 +2k_\parallel^2k^2 / \beta )=0</math>

For Hall MHD:

<math>{\displaystyle (\omega ^{2}-2k_{\parallel }^{2}/\beta )(\omega ^{4}-(2/\beta +1)k^{2}\omega ^{2}+2k_{\parallel }^{2}k^{2}/\beta )-2d_s^2 k_\parallel^2 k^2 \omega^2(\omega^2 - k^2)/ \beta =0}</math>

For QMHD:

<math>{\displaystyle {\displaystyle ((1+2/ \beta c^2)\omega ^{2}-2k_{\parallel }^{2}/\beta )((1+2/ \beta c^2)\omega ^{4}-(2/\beta +1)k^{2}\omega ^{2}+2k_{\parallel }^{2}k^{2}/\beta )-2d_{s}^{2}k_{\parallel }^{2}k^{2}\omega ^{2}(\omega ^{2}-k^{2})/\beta =0}}  </math>

== Examples ==
During the implosion of an [[inertial confinement fusion]] target, the hot shell material surrounding the cold [[deuterium|D]]–[[tritium|T]] fuel layer is shock-accelerated. This instability is also seen in [[magnetized target fusion]] (MTF).<ref>"On the collapse of a Gas Cavity by an Imploding Molten Lead Shell and Richtmyer–Meshkov Instability" Victoria Suponitsky, et al. General Fusion Inc, 2013</ref> Mixing of the shell material and fuel is not desired and efforts are made to minimize any tiny imperfections or irregularities which will be magnified by RMI.

Supersonic combustion in a [[scramjet]] may benefit from RMI as the fuel-oxidants interface is enhanced by the breakup of the fuel into finer droplets.  Also in studies of [[deflagration to detonation transition]] (DDT) processes show that RMI-induced flame acceleration can result in detonation.
